lead: San Bernardino plumbing deals with heat, hard water, older homes and active fault lines. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across San Bernardino.
risk: aging galvanized and cast-iron pipes, slab leaks and water heater strapping
risk_short: old pipes, slab leaks and water heaters
why: Downtown and the North End have homes from the 1910s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron drains and clay sewer laterals. Postwar homes across the city sit on slabs.
The San Andreas and San Jacinto faults run close to the city, so water heaters must be strapped. Summer heat and Santa Ana winds are hard on garage water heaters.
water: San Bernardino pumps nearly all of its water from the Bunker Hill groundwater basin. It is moderately hard.
tips: Strap your water heater for earthquakes.
Keep a wrench by your gas shutoff.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Scope old sewer lines before buying.
areas: PipeMend works Downtown and in the Arrowhead area, Del Rosa, Verdemont, the North End, Hillcrest and every other San Bernardino neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of San Bernardino Building and Safety Division, and plumbing contractors need a CSLB license with a C-36 classification.

faq.q: Why does earthquake safety matter for San Bernardino plumbing?
faq.a: The San Andreas Fault runs along the city's northern edge. Strapped water heaters and flexible gas connectors keep lines from breaking in a quake. Know where your gas and water shutoffs are.
